item.title: #3587565: Static cache entities that aren't loaded
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +130/−11 · php +130/−11
  • Diff: 2ab239c
  • Discussion: #3587565 · 4 contributors · 34 comments
  • Followers: 7

Summary

Entity storage previously had no memory of failed load attempts within a request: if code tried to load an entity ID that doesn't exist (a common case for config entities, such as per-bundle language content settings that not every bundle defines), it would query the persistent cache backend again on every subsequent attempt for that same ID. Now the fact that an ID was not found is also recorded in the per-request static cache, so repeated lookups of the same missing ID skip the cache backend entirely for the rest of the request. Drupal core's performance test suite shows this measurably reduces cache backend reads on real pages: cold-cache node page requests dropped from 225 to 217 cache gets, cold-cache front page requests from 233 to 225, and the administrator node page from 265 to 257 (mostly in the config cache bin), with no change in database query counts.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

In EntityStorageBase::loadMultiple(), after doLoadMultiple() runs, any requested IDs that are still missing are now recorded via a new setNotFoundStaticCache() method, and checked on subsequent calls via getNotFoundFromStaticCache(). Both use a new buildNotFoundCacheId() helper that wraps buildCacheId() with a not_found: prefix, so a storage's own buildCacheId() override (for example ConfigEntityStorage::buildCacheId(), which appends config override keys) is automatically reflected in the not-found cache key too. resetCache() now clears both the entity cache and the not-found cache entries for the given IDs. setStaticCache() was also changed to iterate $entities by its array key (foreach ($entities as $id => $entity)) rather than deriving the cache key from $entity->id(), since the not-found bookkeeping needs to track the originally requested ID.

A new unit test, testLoadMultipleNoResult(), asserts that loading the same nonexistent ID twice in a request results in only a single persistent-cache getMultiple() call. This builds on the earlier bulk-loading work in #3560633 that reduced repeated config entity lookups for per-bundle settings.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: April 29, 2026
  • First commit: August 6, 2026 (3 months later)
  • Last commit: August 9, 2026 (3 days and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • catch (Third and Grove)
  • berdir (MD Systems GmbH)
  • godotislate

Collaboration

catch initially considered adding separate load methods for not-found entities but was concerned it would complicate cache invalidation; noticing that the existing UUID lookup cache already followed a similar pattern, they instead added a distinct not_found: cache key prefix with dedicated get/set methods. During development this approach broke ConfigEntityStorage, which overrides buildCacheId() to append config override keys, catch fixed it by having buildNotFoundCacheId() delegate through buildCacheId() in the base class, so storage-specific overrides are automatically honored without needing their own fix.

item.title: #3614153: Install system module alongside other modules in the installer
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 44 files, +197/−100 · php +197/−90 · yml +0/−10
  • Diff: 6c4592b
  • Discussion: #3614153 · 6 contributors · 35 comments
  • Followers: 7

Summary

Drupal's installer previously installed the System module as its own dedicated step before installing anything else, a pattern that dates back to Drupal's early history. This change installs System alongside the other required modules (and, for profiles that declare modules, alongside those too) in the same batch, eliminating an extra service-container rebuild during every installation. As part of removing the special-casing this required, the core "testing" install profile (used by Drupal's own and many contrib functional tests) no longer automatically enables the page_cache and dynamic_page_cache modules. Tests that rely on those modules being present for cache tag or cache header assertions now need to enable them explicitly. Reported savings were significant, one job's test run time dropped from 90 seconds to well under that, and a full functional test job went from over a minute to about two minutes total.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

Previously drupal_install_system() called module_installer->install(['system'], FALSE) directly as an isolated step, and both install_profile_modules() and install_recipe_required_modules() explicitly filtered system out of the module list they installed afterwards (array_diff(array_unique($modules), ['system'])). Now system is simply left in those module lists and installed together with the rest in the normal batch via _install_module_batch(), cutting one container rebuild out of the install path (and, for profiles with declared modules, another).

Because the default language config write (system.site langcode/default_langcode) used to happen right after installing System in drupal_install_system(), that logic moved into _install_module_batch(), which gained a new $install_state parameter (also threaded through install_profile_modules() and install_recipe_required_modules()) so it can still set the language once system shows up in whichever batch group installs it. Since the service container can now be compiled before System module (and its config) exists, DrupalKernel::compileContainer() gained a fallback that reads $GLOBALS['install_state']['parameters']['langcode'] to seed language.default_values when system.site config isn't available yet; this is flagged with a @todo as a temporary workaround pending moving default-language config out of System module entirely (tracked in #3337864).

install_config_import_batch() no longer needs to copy the site UUID from the sync storage into the freshly-created system.site config (the "UUID juggle"), because System module's config is now imported directly rather than being created fresh and then overwritten. Correspondingly, ConfigImporter::validateSiteUuid() now returns TRUE when there's no target system.site config yet, since that indicates a fresh install-from-config rather than a UUID mismatch.

The testing.info.yml/testing_multilingual.info.yml profiles' install: keys for drupal:page_cache and dynamic_page_cache were removed, and many core functional test classes (JSON:API, REST, Views, Block, error/session tests, etc.) were updated to add page_cache and/or dynamic_page_cache to their $modules property, or install them at runtime, wherever the test actually depends on page or dynamic-page caching behavior. This groundwork is what makes #3428372, open for over fifteen years, finally achievable, and several immediate follow-ups were spun off: #3615455 (install database driver modules alongside others), #3614401 (allow install profiles to opt out of being installed), #3614825 (allow additional modules to be installed alongside profile modules), and #3614817 (reduce parallel functional test jobs given the speedup).

Upgrade

If your module's functional tests rely on Drupal core's "testing" install profile having page_cache or dynamic_page_cache enabled by default (for example, to assert cache tags/contexts or X-Drupal-Cache headers), add them explicitly to the test class:

protected static $modules = [
  'your_module',
  'page_cache',
  'dynamic_page_cache',
];

or install them at runtime where needed:

\Drupal::service('module_installer')->install(['page_cache']);

This change is only present on Drupal core's main branch (targeting Drupal 12) and was not backported to 10.x/11.x.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: July 31, 2026
  • Committed: August 7, 2026 (7 days later)

Key contributors

  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)
  • nicxvan (nLightened Development LLC)
  • mstrelan (PreviousNext)
  • godotislate
  • amateescu

Collaboration

catch did the initial profiling and iterative work, tracking down a "three line hack" needed in DrupalKernel for the default language to survive the reordering, and progressively removing special-casing of the System module across the installer and tests. mstrelan's review caught remaining stray page_cache/dynamic_page_cache uninstalls in SessionTest and DisplayFeedTest and questioned whether install_recipe_required_modules() could still assume System was already installed, prompting further fixes. During a later review, amateescu found that _install_module_batch() still needed to rely on $install_state and reverted a commit that had removed that dependency, adding test coverage to lock in the requirement. godotislate then suggested an approach to avoid passing $install_state around further and flagged an unresolved @todo; catch applied the suggestions, opened a follow-up issue for the @todo (referenced in the AssertPageCacheContextsAndTagsTrait::enablePageCaching cleanup discussion), and godotislate ultimately committed the change.

item.title: #3593485: Use YamlCacheCollectorDiscovery for links, tasks, and actions
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 8 files, +123/−198 · php +111/−195 · yml +12/−3
  • Diff: 42747ab
  • Discussion: #3593485 · 5 contributors · 26 comments
  • Followers: 7

Summary

Drupal now reuses parsed menu link, local task, and local action YAML definitions across cache clears instead of re-parsing the underlying .links.menu.yml, .links.task.yml, and .links.action.yml files from every module on each cache rebuild. This follows up on the file-parsing cache collector introduced in #3486503 and shaves measurable time off cold-cache page requests (profiling on an Umami install showed roughly a net 12ms saving per cold-cache request from this change alone, out of a total ~90ms available from YAML parsing overall), with bigger gains expected on sites with more modules.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: Constructing MenuLinkManager, LocalActionManager, or LocalTaskManager without the new $yaml_cache_collector argument is deprecated in Drupal 11.5.0 and will be required in Drupal 12.0.0.

Technical details

MenuLinkManager, LocalActionManager, and LocalTaskManager each get a new YamlCacheCollectorDiscovery (in Drupal\Core\Plugin\Discovery) in place of the plain YamlDiscovery they previously used in getDiscovery(). This new discovery class wraps the component-level Drupal\Core\Discovery\YamlCacheCollectorDiscovery with a Drupal\Core\Utility\YamlCacheCollector instance, so parsed YAML definitions persist in the cache.file_parsing bin rather than being reparsed from disk on every cache rebuild.

Three new services back this: menu_link.yaml_cache_collector, local_action.yaml_cache_collector, and local_task.yaml_cache_collector, each a Drupal\Core\Utility\YamlCacheCollector keyed to menu.link.yaml, menu.local_action.yaml, or menu.local_task.yaml respectively, using @cache.file_parsing, @lock, and @datetime.time. The three manager constructors were converted to promoted properties and gained a new optional ?CacheCollectorInterface $yaml_cache_collector = NULL parameter; when omitted, each manager triggers an E_USER_DEPRECATED notice and falls back to pulling the corresponding collector service directly from the container via \Drupal::service().

Existing kernel performance tests (PageCacheTest/related TestFrontPageColdCache, testNodePageColdCache, doTestNodePageAdministrator) had their expected CacheGetCount and per-bin file_parsing counts bumped by one to account for the new collector's cache lookup.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">Code that instantiates MenuLinkManager, LocalActionManager, or LocalTaskManager directly (for example in a custom service definition that decorates or replaces one of these) should pass the new argument to avoid the deprecation notice:

public function __construct(
  MenuTreeStorageInterface $tree_storage,
  StaticMenuLinkOverridesInterface $overrides,
  ModuleHandlerInterface $module_handler,
  ?CacheCollectorInterface $yaml_cache_collector = NULL,
) {

Pass the matching core service (menu_link.yaml_cache_collector, local_action.yaml_cache_collector, or local_task.yaml_cache_collector) as the new argument in your service definition's arguments list.

  • Last commit: August 5, 2026 (1 day and 2 commits later)

item.title: #1945262: Introduce "before" and "after" for conditional ordering in library definitions
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Major task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 24 files, +245/−365 · php +145/−291 · yml +96/−72 · js +4/−2
  • Diff: f9289ba
  • Discussion: #1945262 · 25 contributors · 184 comments
  • Followers: 98

Summary

Drupal's asset library system now lets a library declare that it must load before or after another library, in addition to the existing dependencies key. This gives module and theme authors a reliable way to control asset ordering for cases where a real dependency relationship doesn't exist (for example, a library that only reacts to another library if it happens to be present), without resorting to fragile per-file weight values or custom hook_js_alter()/hook_css_alter() code. As part of this change, many long-standing weight overrides and ordering workarounds in core library definitions (jQuery UI assets, contextual, views, settings_tray, CKEditor 5 translations, locale, form_test, and others) were replaced with explicit dependencies, before, or after declarations, or removed outright where dependencies already implied the correct order.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: Asset library definitions in *.libraries.yml now support before and after keys, listing other libraries that must load after or before the declaring library, respectively.

Technical details

The core mechanism for resolving library load order was rewritten around a directed graph instead of ad hoc weight math. LibraryDependencyResolver::doGetDependencies() now builds a graph of libraries and their dependencies as edges, doProcessBeforeAfter() adds extra edges for any before/after keys found in each library's definition (only when the referenced library is already part of the graph), and getLibrariesWithDependencies() runs the result through Drupal\Component\Graph\Graph::searchAndSort() and then sorts by the resulting weight to produce the final load order. getMinimalRepresentativeSubset() was similarly reworked to use the graph's edges rather than repeatedly calling getLibrariesWithDependencies().

AssetResolver::getCssAssets() and getJsAssets() no longer nudge weights by count($css) / 30000 to preserve insertion order; instead they skip re-adding an asset file that has already been added, so the first occurrence (which reflects the correct dependency/before/after order) wins. ckeditor5_js_alter() no longer manipulates a synthetic weight to group translation files for aggregation, it just filters out translation files that don't match the current language via array_filter(). Similarly, locale_js_alter() no longer sets a weight to force the translation file to load first, and settings_tray drops its cssAlter() hook and group: 200 override in favor of an after: [core/drupal.dialog] declaration.

Several core libraries were updated to use before/after: drupal.contextual-links now declares before: [contextual/drupal.context-toolbar], drupal.vertical-tabs gets before: [core/drupal.collapse] (moved from form_test's own weight hack), and test fixture libraries (common_test, js_testing_ajax_request_test) were added to exercise the new keys directly.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: March 17, 2013
  • First commit: August 3, 2026 (13 years later)
  • Last commit: August 5, 2026 (1 day and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • nod_ (Eclipse Foundation)
  • robloach (Kalamuna)
  • sun
  • webchick
  • catch (Third and Grove)
  • penyaskito
  • amol_tatkare
  • taran2l (Lemberg Solutions)
  • smustgrave (Mobomo)
  • luenemann (FlexiFlow GmbH)
  • wim leers (Acquia)
  • liam morland (OpenPlus)
  • neclimdul (APQC)
  • godotislate

Collaboration

This task sat open for over a decade, blocked mainly on how to remove per-file weight overrides without breaking ordering guarantees that weights had been silently providing. wim leers repeatedly identified edge cases where dependency declarations alone couldn't express the needed ordering (contextual.toolbar.js needing to run after contextual.js without formally depending on it, and the analogous tour.js/overlay case), which is what motivated the before/after design discussed with sdboyer and nod_ back in comment #4. Early attempts to remove weights outright (nod_'s and penyaskito's patches) were committed and then reverted by webchick after wim leers reported breakage on /admin/config/development/testing, and wim leers's review in comment #38 caught several library comments that would have become lies (contextual.js, views-contextual.js) had the weights simply been dropped without replacement ordering guarantees. The eventual approach, proposed by wim leers in comment #76 (keep weights for BC while adding before/after, then deprecate weights separately), matched what catch suggested and was later implemented by taran2l in the merge request, building on nod_'s earlier groundwork of adding before keys without yet acting on them.

item.title: #3411490: Replace array-based DB Schema API with a value object structure
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 30 files, +2436/−288 · php +2435/−288 · txt +1
  • Diff: 689e585
  • Discussion: #3411490 · 15 contributors · 139 comments
  • Followers: 29

Summary

Drupal now offers a second, object-oriented way to define database table structures for hook_schema() and similar schema-defining code, alongside the traditional nested associative array. Instead of building a $schema['mytable'] = ['fields' => [...], 'primary key' => [...]] array, module developers can construct a Table object made up of Column, Index, PrimaryKey, UniqueKey, and ForeignKey value objects. These objects validate their own arguments when created (for example, rejecting a length argument on an int column, or a string default on a numeric column), which surfaces schema definition mistakes immediately instead of failing later or silently producing a wrong table. This is purely additive: existing hook_schema() implementations that return arrays keep working exactly as before, nothing needs to change immediately. Core's own conversion of its hook_schema() implementations to the new objects is being done incrementally in follow-up issues.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New Drupal\Core\Database\SchemaDefinition namespace (Table, Column, Index, PrimaryKey, UniqueKey, ForeignKey, Schema, plus ColumnType/ColumnSize/SchemaDefinitionType enums) and Schema::createSchemaFromDefinition()/createTableFromDefinition() for defining database table structures as an alternative to nested arrays.

Technical details

The new value objects live under Drupal\Core\Database\SchemaDefinition and are immutable and database-abstract: Table holds columns, primaryKey, uniqueKeys, indexes, foreignKeys, and description; Column carries type (ColumnType enum: Char, Varchar, VarcharAscii, Text, Int, Serial, Float, Numeric, Blob), size (ColumnSize enum), and validated modifiers like length, unsigned, precision/scale, binary, serialize. Column defaults are typed StringValue|IntValue|FloatValue|NullValue|null, which lets the API distinguish "no default specified" (PHP null, the argument omitted) from "the default is explicitly NULL" (new NullValue()), a distinction the array API could not make cleanly. Every object exposes toArray(), converting itself back to the legacy array shape, so Schema::createTable() and the database drivers do not need to change at all: Schema::createSchemaFromDefinition(Schema $schema) and the new final createTableFromDefinition() method simply call $table->toArray() under the hood. Constructor-time validation throws SchemaDefinitionException (a DatabaseException) for invalid combinations, e.g. notNull on a Serial column, unsigned on a non-numeric column, or a NULL default combined with notNull: TRUE.

ModuleHandler::installSchema()/uninstallSchema() were updated to accept either an array or a Schema object back from hook_schema(), so both styles can coexist during migration. Drupal\Core\Batch\BatchStorage::schemaDefinition() and locale_schema() were converted as worked examples, along with the hook_schema() documentation in database.api.php. A SchemaDefinitionType enum (Module, Storage, Entity, Migrate, Test) tags where a Schema came from, anticipating a future registry of abstract schema definitions discussed in the issue. Extensibility for database-driver-specific needs (e.g. PostgreSQL GIN/GIST indexes) is handled via a dbSpecificExtra array property on Column/Table/Index rather than by subclassing, since the value object classes are final. Follow-ups #3557481 (converting core's hook_schema() implementations) and #3568040 (converting storage classes' ensureTableExists() methods) build directly on this API.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">No action is required: existing hook_schema() implementations returning arrays continue to work unchanged. To opt in to the new API, return a Schema object instead, for example (adapted from the updated hook_schema() documentation):

function hook_schema(): Schema {
  $tables[] = new Table(
    name: 'users_data',
    description: 'Stores module data as key/value pairs per user.',
    columns: [
      Column::int(
        name: 'uid',
        description: 'The {users}.uid this record affects.',
        unsigned: TRUE,
        notNull: TRUE,
        default: new IntValue(0),
      ),
      Column::varcharAscii(
        name: 'name',
        description: 'The identifier of the data.',
        length: 128,
        notNull: TRUE,
        default: new StringValue(''),
      ),
    ],
    primaryKey: new PrimaryKey(['uid', 'name']),
    indexes: [
      new Index(name: 'name', columns: ['name']),
    ],
  );

  return new Schema(
    type: SchemaDefinitionType::Module,
    name: 'hook',
    tables: $tables,
  );
}

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: December 31, 2023
  • First commit: August 2, 2026 (2 years later)
  • Last commit: August 4, 2026 (1 day and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • mondrake
  • daffie
  • geek-merlin (Geeks4Change)
  • mradcliffe (Kosada)
  • alexpott (Acro Commerce)
  • joachim (Chicken)
  • catch (Third and Grove)
  • amateescu
  • larowlan (PreviousNext)

Collaboration

The design went through substantial back and forth on how to keep the value objects extensible without sacrificing type safety. Daffie flagged that making Column/Table/Index final would block the PostgreSQL driver from adding GIN/GIST index support (#3397622); mondrake held that db-specific concerns belong outside this "abstract" schema layer, and the two converged on adding a dbSpecificExtra property (an indexes extra array key when converted to the legacy shape) rather than removing final or allowing subclassing. geek-merlin separately proposed keying such extras by class-string for better static-analysis inference, which mondrake acknowledged as useful for a future iteration. Alexpott pushed to keep the legacy array output completely untouched by this issue and questioned an early Property::Undefined sentinel; mondrake replaced it with dedicated StringValue/IntValue/FloatValue/NullValue wrapper objects so that "no default given" and "default is explicitly NULL" could be distinguished without a special enum case.

item.title: #3604286: Upsert - Allow to customize the behavior of the update when the insert fails and use more Upsert queries in core
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 13 files, +283/−32 · php +283/−32
  • Diff: 047e314
  • Discussion: #3604286 · 3 contributors · 34 comments
  • Followers: 5

Summary

Drupal's database Upsert query (insert-or-update in one statement) previously always fell back to overwriting a row with the values that were meant to be inserted whenever the insert half of the operation hit an existing key. There was no way to say "update this column based on its current value" (for example, incrementing a counter atomically). This change extends Upsert so a per-column update expression can be supplied, and several core subsystems that previously used the older, less efficient Merge query (which does a separate select plus insert/update) were converted to use it: cache tag invalidation counters, file usage counts, and the search index word score. As a bonus, cache tag invalidations, and the other converted operations, now happen in a single atomic database round trip instead of two.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New Drupal\Core\Database\Expression value object and Drupal\Core\Database\Query\UpsertUpdateExpression subclass let an Upsert query run a column specific SQL expression (e.g. incrementing a counter) instead of overwriting the column with the insert value when a row already exists.

Technical details

The core addition is Drupal\Core\Database\Expression, a simple value object holding an expression string plus keyed arguments, and Drupal\Core\Database\Query\UpsertUpdateExpression, a thin subclass of it used specifically for upsert update overrides. Upsert::fields() was extended so entries can mix plain column names (for the insert list) with column => new UpsertUpdateExpression(...) pairs; the latter are collected into a new $updateExpressions property and their arguments are merged into the bound query parameters in execute(). If fields() receives an associative array mixing plain insert values with an UpsertUpdateExpression, or an expression entry without a string column key, it throws \InvalidArgumentException.

Each driver's Upsert::__toString() (mysql's ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE, pgsql's and sqlite's ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE) now substitutes the raw expression for a column instead of VALUES($field) / EXCLUDED.$field when one was supplied. The mysql driver's execute() binds expression arguments with bindValue() rather than bindParam(), since by-reference binding inside a loop would make every placeholder share the same final loop variable.

Using this, Drupal\Core\Cache\CacheTagsChecksum::doInvalidateTags(), Drupal\file\FileUsage\DatabaseFileUsageBackend::add(), and search_index word scoring in search.module were converted from merge()/expression() to upsert() with an UpsertUpdateExpression for the incrementing column. Conversions of Drupal\Core\KeyValueStore\DatabaseStorage, StringDatabaseStorage, and TaxonomyHooks were explicitly left out of scope, per discussion in the issue, and remain on Merge. hook_entity_predelete() and hook_ENTITY_TYPE_predelete() example code in core/lib/Drupal/Core/Entity/entity.api.php was updated to demonstrate the Upsert equivalent of the old Merge pattern.

Upgrade

Custom code using Merge purely to emulate an atomic counter or expression based update can switch to Upsert with an UpsertUpdateExpression, for example:

$connection->upsert('example_deleted_entity_statistics')
  ->key(['type', 'id'])
  ->fields([
    'type',
    'id',
    'count' => new UpsertUpdateExpression('{example_deleted_entity_statistics}.[count] + :count', [':count' => $count]),
  ])
  ->values([
    'type' => $type,
    'id' => $id,
    'count' => $count,
  ])
  ->execute();

This is not a breaking change: Upsert::fields() remains backward compatible for plain column/value usage.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: June 19, 2026
  • Committed: August 4, 2026 (1 month and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • mondrake
  • daffie
  • amateescu

Collaboration

During review, mondrake found and reverted an in-progress attempt to also convert StringDatabaseStorage, after discovering it produced duplicate key errors from a unique index added on all non lid columns, deciding to leave that conversion for a separate follow-up. The design of the update expression API itself changed mid-review: mondrake initially attached the expression to the insert values, then realized that didn't work when a single upsert call queues multiple value sets, and reworked it so the expression is specified once per column alongside the field list instead. Later, amateescu's review caught an actual bug in the mysql driver's parameter binding (bindParam() versus bindValue()), which mondrake fixed by binding by value to avoid all placeholders sharing the same loop variable reference.

item.title: #3565258: Support library-specific aggregates
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Major task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 27 files, +624/−116 · php +573/−102 · yml +51/−14
  • Diff: d9cc509
  • Discussion: #3565258 · 9 contributors · 122 comments
  • Followers: 23

Summary

Drupal's asset library system can now mark specific CSS or JavaScript libraries so their files are always bundled into their own aggregate, regardless of which other libraries happen to be attached on a given page. Previously, the exact set of libraries in an aggregate, and therefore its URL and query string, varied depending on everything else loaded on that particular page, so browsers and CDNs often re-downloaded effectively the same CSS or JS just because the query string differed slightly from page to page. By setting the new aggregate_target key on a library, its aggregate gets a predictable, page-independent URL, which increases browser and CDN cache hit rates for repeat and multi-page visits. Core has already applied this to several always-loaded libraries (core/drupal, core/drupalSettings, system/base, parts of Umami and Claro) and switched some small vendor JS libraries to preprocess: false instead, since aggregating a single already-minified file offers no benefit.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: AssetResolverInterface::getCssAssets() and ::getJsAssets() gained an optional $with_dependencies parameter (default TRUE); custom implementations of the interface must add it to stay compatible.
  • New API: New aggregate_target library definition key (with css and js sub-keys, each accepting true or an arbitrary string) forces a library's assets into a dedicated, page-independent aggregate.

Technical details

Library definitions can now declare aggregate_target: {css: ..., js: ...}, where the value is either true (unique per library) or an arbitrary string shared by several libraries meant to be co-located. LibraryDiscoveryParser::buildByExtension() normalizes this to ['css' => FALSE, 'js' => FALSE] when absent, and also records each CSS file's SMACSS category so it can be checked later. CssCollectionGrouper::group() and JsCollectionGrouper::group() track, per group, whether all files belonging to a targeted library (and, for CSS, a given category) landed contiguously in a single group via a $first_seen_libraries/$seen_index mechanism; if a library's files get split across groups because of per-file weights or other libraries interleaving, the libraries key is dropped from those groups and the aggregate silently falls back to the pre-existing include/exclude/delta behavior.

When a group does carry a libraries key, CssCollectionOptimizerLazy::optimize() and JsCollectionOptimizerLazy::optimize() build the asset URL using a compressed libraries query argument (and, for CSS, a category argument, since a single library can still span multiple categories) instead of include/exclude/delta.     js: 'mygroup'

  js:

item.title: #3524971: Defend against \GuzzleHttp\Cookie\FileCookieJar gadget chain
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 4 files, +304/−3 · php +299 · lock +3/−2 · json +2/−1

Summary

Drupal 11.x now ships a hardened replacement for Guzzle's \GuzzleHttp\Cookie\FileCookieJar class, closing off a publicly known "gadget chain" that can be abused to write an arbitrary file to the server. On its own this class isn't reachable by an attacker, it only becomes dangerous if a site (core or, more likely, a contrib or custom module) also has a PHP Object Injection vulnerability that lets attacker-controlled data reach unserialize(). With this fix in place, even if such a vulnerability existed elsewhere, this particular gadget chain would no longer be usable to write files. This is defense in depth, not a fix for a standalone vulnerability, and requires no action from site owners beyond updating.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Security: Backports Guzzle 8.0's hardening of \GuzzleHttp\Cookie\FileCookieJar (a private autoSave flag disabled by __wakeup()) into an early-loaded shim, closing a PHP Object Injection-chained arbitrary file write gadget on Drupal 11.x. Not independently exploitable; requires a separate deserialization vulnerability.

Technical details

The underlying issue is in Guzzle itself: FileCookieJar::__destruct() calls save(), which writes $this->filename to disk. If an attacker can get arbitrary serialized data into unserialize() (via some other PHP Object Injection bug), they can craft a FileCookieJar instance with an attacker-chosen $filename and cookie payload; when PHP garbage-collects it, __destruct() writes that payload to the attacker's chosen path, a classic deserialization file-write gadget (documented in PHPGGC's Guzzle/FW/1 chain). Guzzle's maintainers eventually landed a fix for Guzzle 8.0 (https://github.com/guzzle/guzzle/pull/3334) adding a private $autoSave flag that __wakeup() sets to false and __destruct() checks before saving, so an unserialized instance never persists to disk. Drupal core was still on Guzzle 7.x, which lacks this hardening.

Rather than removing or aliasing the class (approaches discussed earlier in the issue, including using the core.moved_classes mechanism from #3502882), the committed fix backports the Guzzle 8.0 hardened implementation verbatim into a new core/includes/guzzle_file_cookie_jar_shim.php, registered in composer.json's autoload.files list alongside bootstrap.inc. Composer's files autoload entries are required unconditionally and very early, before PSR-4 autoloading for anything else kicks in, so this shim's class GuzzleHttp\Cookie\FileCookieJar (guarded by a class_exists(..., false) check) gets declared first and pre-empts the classloader from ever loading Guzzle's own, unhardened copy of the file. The shim preserves full functionality, normal instantiation still auto-saves on __destruct(), but any instance produced via unserialize() has autoSave forced to false by __wakeup(), so the file-write gadget is inert. This is a temporary measure: the @todo in the shim notes it should be removed once Drupal updates to Guzzle 8, which already happened on the main branch in #3612544; this fix was committed only to the 11.x branch since it will still be supported for some time and the composer.json changes did not backport cleanly to older branches.

Timeline

  • Opened: May 16, 2025
  • Committed: August 4, 2026 (1 year later)

Key contributors

  • catch (Third and Grove)

The approach evolved considerably over the issue's life. mcdruid initially explored removing the class from the autoloader or aliasing it via the core.moved_classes mechanism from #3502882, but found in testing that if the original vendor file was still present on disk, PHP would still autoload the real class instead of the alias, undermining that approach. cmlara pushed back on the earlier "just remove it" direction, pointing out that auditing only Drupal-namespace contrib code for usage risks false negatives since the class could be used anywhere in a site's full dependency stack, and that removing the class without a replacement risked white-screen-of-death failures for sites that do legitimately use it. item.title: #3607968: Promote defaults._title to top level in route attributes
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 17 files, +415/−47 · php +415/−37 · yml +0/−10

  • Followers: 6

Summary

Following up on the introduction of PHP attributes for route discovery (#3311365), Drupal core now provides its own #[Route] attribute that extends Symfony's, adding a top level title property. Previously, setting a page title on an attribute-based route required nesting it inside defaults: ['_title' => ...]; now it can be written as title: new TranslatableMarkup('...') directly on the attribute. The new attribute also supports closures for dynamic titles, letting modules avoid writing a separate _title_callback controller method just to compute a title. This is a developer-facing convenience change with no end-user visible effect, aside from the many core routes (system.module's admin pages, block content add form, etc.) that were converted to use it.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: BlockContentController::getAddFormTitle() is deprecated in favor of a title closure on the route attribute.
  • New API: New title property on Drupal's #[Route] attribute (Drupal\Core\Routing\Attribute\Route, extending Symfony's), accepting a string, TranslatableMarkup, or closure for the page title.

Technical details

The new Drupal\Core\Routing\Attribute\Route class extends Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route and, in its constructor, moves a passed title argument into $this->defaults['_title']. Passing both title and a _title default simultaneously trips an assertion. Because closures cannot be serialized into the router table, AttributeRouteDiscovery::getAttributes() detects a closure title and replaces it in the stored defaults with a _title_closure reference tuple of [class, method, index] (the index disambiguates multiple #[Route] attributes on the same method). TitleResolver::getTitle() was updated to recognize _title_closure and resolve the actual closure at render time via the new static method Route::getTitleClosure(), which re-reflects the method's attributes to retrieve the closure (since it can't be persisted) and resolves controller arguments the same way _title_callback does, except without container access.

All core routes previously using defaults: ['_title' => ...] on attribute-based routes were converted to the top level title property, including the system.module admin controllers and SiteInformationForm. BlockContentController::addForm()'s route was converted to use a closure title (title: static function (BlockContentTypeInterface $block_content_type) {...}), and its old getAddFormTitle() method was deprecated for removal in Drupal 13.0.0, with the accompanying block_content.add_form YAML route definition removed since discovery now happens purely through the attribute.

Upgrade

Modules converting *.routing.yml route definitions to #[Route] attributes (per #3311365) can now write, instead of:

#[Route(
  path: '/admin/config/system/site-information',
  name: 'system.site_information_settings',
  requirements: ['_permission' => 'administer site configuration'],
  defaults: ['_title' => new TranslatableMarkup('Basic site settings')],
)]

the shorter:

#[Route(
  path: '/admin/config/system/site-information',
  name: 'system.site_information_settings',
  title: new TranslatableMarkup('Basic site settings'),
  requirements: ['_permission' => 'administer site configuration'],
)]

For dynamic titles that don't need injected services, a closure can replace a separate _title_callback method:

#[Route(
  path: '/block/add/{block_content_type}',
  name: 'block_content.add_form',
  title: static function (BlockContentTypeInterface $block_content_type) {
    return new TranslatableMarkup('Add %type content block', ['%type' => $block_content_type->label()]);
  },
  requirements: ['_entity_create_access' => 'block_content:{block_content_type}'],
)]

Code calling Drupal\block_content\Controller\BlockContentController::getAddFormTitle() should stop using it before Drupal 13.0.0.

This led longwave to add closure support directly to the #[Route] attribute and solve the "which attribute" ambiguity by recording an [class, method, index] reference during route discovery. godotislate reviewed the resulting MR, confirmed the route discovery skip-file logic still worked with the new attribute, and catch merged it, noting it was "soft-blocking a lot of route conversions from YAML."

Summary

Drupal's database transaction system has, since its inception, committed a transaction automatically when the PHP Transaction object holding it went out of scope and was garbage collected. This implicit "commit on destruct" behavior is now deprecated: code should instead call $transaction->commitOrRelease() explicitly once the wrapped database operations have completed. The old behavior still works for now (it's removed only in Drupal 13.0.0), so most sites and contributed modules will keep working unchanged, but developers writing custom code that opens transactions directly should update it to avoid deprecation notices and to avoid relying on PHP's unpredictable object destruction order. A few internal helper methods added earlier as a workaround for this same destruction-order problem (Connection::commitAll(), Database::commitAllOnShutdown(), TransactionManagerBase::commitAll()) are also deprecated with no replacement, since they exist only to support the mechanism being phased out.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: Implicit commit of a Transaction object on destruction is deprecated (removed in Drupal 13.0.0). Also deprecated for removal: Connection::commitAll(), Database::commitAllOnShutdown(), TransactionManagerBase::commitAll(), with no replacement.

Technical details

TransactionManagerBase::purge(), called when a Transaction object's destructor runs, now emits @trigger_error(..., E_USER_DEPRECATED) pointing to Transaction::commitOrRelease() as the replacement, unless a new private $exceptionThrown flag is set. That flag is set whenever push(), unpile(), commit(), rollback(), addPostTransactionCallback(), or processRootCommit() throws (TransactionNameNonUniqueException, TransactionOutOfOrderException, TransactionCommitFailedException, LogicException), so that objects destroyed during exception unwinding don't produce a spurious deprecation notice, and is reset to FALSE whenever a new root transaction begins. TransactionManagerBase::commitAll(), Connection::commitAll(), and Database::commitAllOnShutdown() are marked @deprecated in drupal:11.5.0 ... removed from drupal:13.0.0 using only doc-comment deprecation (no @trigger_error), since these run implicitly on every request shutdown and would otherwise flood deprecation logs; PHPStan (@phpstan-ignore) is relied on instead to catch remaining usages statically.

Separately, ContentEntityStorageBase::save() now catches \Throwable instead of \Exception around the save operation before rolling back its transaction. Per mondrake's comment on the issue, the narrower \Exception catch could let a PHP Error escape without rolling back, leaving the transaction to be released (committed) via destruction instead of rolled back, exactly the kind of bug this deprecation effort is meant to surface and prevent.

Class doc comments on Transaction and Connection were updated to no longer describe destruction-triggered commit as the intended usage pattern, directing developers toward calling commitOrRelease() explicitly instead. try {
  $transaction = \Drupal::database()->startTransaction();
  // ... perform database operations ...
  my_other_function($id);

  // The transaction has completed, commit it here.
  $transaction->commitOrRelease();

  return $id;
}
catch (Exception $e) {
  $transaction->rollback();
  throw $e;
}

Do not call Connection::commitAll(), Database::commitAllOnShutdown(), or TransactionManagerBase::commitAll(): they are deprecated with no replacement and will be removed in Drupal 13.0.0.

Summary

Drupal previously blocked changes to a node's menu settings (parent, weight, or removing the menu link) while editing a pending, non-default revision by attaching a validation constraint directly to the node entity type. Because that constraint ran on every save of a node, not just form submissions, it could reject unrelated saves made through code that doesn't go through the node edit form, such as JSON API or REST requests, or programmatic saves during content moderation workflows (as reported in #3048698). This entity-level check has been removed. The same protection now runs only as part of the node add/edit form's validation, so saving a node's menu settings through other means, such as web services or custom code, is no longer restricted by this rule.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: MenuSettingsConstraint and MenuSettingsConstraintValidator are deprecated in drupal:11.5.0 for removal in drupal:13.0.0; the check they performed moved to MenuUiHooks::formNodeFormValidate().

Technical details

The check lived in MenuSettingsConstraint/MenuSettingsConstraintValidator, added to the node entity type unconditionally in MenuUiHooks::entityTypeBuild(). Since $entity->menu is only populated by menu_ui_node_builder() during a node form submission, the constraint's logic was effectively meaningless outside that context, which is what #3048698 and #3010750 ran into.

item.title: #3209204: Adding existing translation throws "Invalid translation language specified"
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core

  • Changes: 2 files, +96/−1 · php +96/−1

Summary

Content editors could get a fatal PHP error ("Invalid translation language specified", a 500 error page) simply by opening the "Add translation" link for a language that had already been translated, for example by clicking it in two browser tabs, or navigating back after saving a translation. This was easy to hit in ordinary editing workflows for both content entities and menu links. The fix makes ContentTranslationController::add() detect that the target translation already exists before building the add form, and instead shows the message "A translation already exists for [language]" and redirects the editor to the existing translation's edit form.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The crash happened because ContentTranslationController::add() unconditionally cloned the entity and called addTranslation() for the target language, which throws an InvalidArgumentException in ContentEntityBase::addTranslation() if that translation already exists. This could occur through races such as two open tabs each adding the same translation, a browser "back" navigation returning to a stale add-translation URL, or another user saving the same translation concurrently.

The fix adds a guard in add(): if $entity->hasTranslation($target->getId()) is true, it calls $this->messenger()->addError() with a translated message and returns a Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\RedirectResponse to $entity->getTranslation($target->getId())->toUrl('edit-form')->toString() instead of proceeding to build the form. The method's return type was widened from array to array|\Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\RedirectResponse to reflect this. A new kernel test, ContentTranslationConcurrencyTest, exercises this by creating an entity with an existing French translation and calling the controller's add() method directly, asserting a redirect response and the error message text.

item.title: #3590917: Introduce a common ancestor class to all Core base test classes
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 8 files, +114/−77 · php +114/−77
  • Diff: fc3581f
  • Discussion: #3590917 · 5 contributors · 17 comments
  • Followers: 7

Summary

Drupal core's PHPUnit test base classes, UnitTestCase, KernelTestBase, BrowserTestBase, and Drupal\BuildTests\Framework\BuildTestBase, now all extend a single common ancestor, Drupal\Tests\DrupalTestCase, instead of each separately extending PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase and using DrupalTestCaseTrait. For the vast majority of unit, kernel, functional, functional-javascript, and build tests in contrib and custom code, which extend one of these existing base classes, nothing changes. The change mainly matters if you write PHPUnit tests for a Drupal\Component library that extend PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase directly (as is required, since Component code must not depend on Core code): if such a test wants Drupal's PHPUnit extensions, it now has to import DrupalTestCaseTrait explicitly rather than getting it automatically.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: The already-deprecated getDrupalRoot() method moved from DrupalTestCaseTrait to DrupalTestCase and lost its static modifier, becoming a regular instance method.
  • New API: New abstract Drupal\Tests\DrupalTestCase class is the common ancestor of UnitTestCase, KernelTestBase, BrowserTestBase and Drupal\BuildTests\Framework\BuildTestBase.

Technical details

Previously, UnitTestCase, KernelTestBase, BrowserTestBase, and BuildTestBase each independently extended PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase and separately used DrupalTestCaseTrait for shared behavior, most notably setting the $root property via a #[Before(100)]-tagged setUpRoot() hook and exposing the deprecated getDrupalRoot() accessor. The new Drupal\Tests\DrupalTestCase abstract class centralizes that: it extends PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase, uses DrupalTestCaseTrait once, and declares the $root property, setUpRoot(), and getDrupalRoot() itself. All four base classes now extend DrupalTestCase instead of TestCase directly, and dropped their own use DrupalTestCaseTrait; statements.

DrupalTestCaseTrait itself was trimmed down to the remaining cross-cutting helpers (such as registering the dumper CLI handler) and re-documented as something you only need to import directly when writing a Drupal\Component test that extends PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase and still wants Drupal's PHPUnit extensions. As part of moving getDrupalRoot() onto DrupalTestCase, it dropped the static modifier it had on the trait, since $this->root is an instance property.

Upgrade

If you maintain a Drupal\Component PHPUnit test that extends PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase directly and relies on Drupal's PHPUnit extensions (previously available for free via DrupalTestCaseTrait), import the trait explicitly:

use Drupal\Tests\DrupalTestCaseTrait;
use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;

class MyComponentTest extends TestCase {
  use DrupalTestCaseTrait;
}

Tests that already extend UnitTestCase, KernelTestBase, BrowserTestBase, or BuildTestBase require no changes.

Summary

Drupal 12 removes the update_fetch_with_http_fallback setting, which previously let a site fall back to plain HTTP when HTTPS requests to updates.drupal.org failed while checking for available updates or security advisories. This insecure fallback option was deprecated in Drupal 11.5 (#3591513) and is now gone with no replacement. Sites that still have this setting uncommented in settings.php should remove it; it no longer has any effect and update/security-advisory checks will always use HTTPS.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Drupal\update\UpdateFetcher::__construct() and Drupal\Core\Update\SecurityAdvisoriesFetcher::__construct() no longer accept a Settings argument; the internal Drupal\package_manager\Validator\SettingsValidator class and its service definition were removed entirely.

Technical details

The change strips the update_fetch_with_http_fallback handling out of the two places that read it: Drupal\update\UpdateFetcher::doRequest() and Drupal\Core\Update\SecurityAdvisoriesFetcher::doRequest() (formerly Drupal\system\SecurityAdvisories\SecurityAdvisoriesFetcher) now issue a single HTTPS GET and no longer catch a failed HTTPS attempt to retry over http://. Both classes' constructors drop the injected Settings $settings parameter along with the $withHttpFallback property. The corresponding entry in Drupal\Core\Site\Settings::$deprecatedSettings is removed, leaving that array empty.

// After:

item.title: #3585886: Outdated _method requirement in CsrfRequestHeaderAccessCheck::applies()
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 5 files, +67/−32 · php +57/−30 · yml +10/−2
  • Diff: 831ce14
  • Discussion: #3585886 · 5 contributors · 12 comments
  • Followers: 6

Summary

CsrfRequestHeaderAccessCheck, the service that decides which routes need the X-CSRF-Token header check, used an outdated way of detecting which HTTP methods a route allows. It looked for the legacy _method route requirement to decide whether a route was read-only (and could skip the check), but modern routes declare allowed methods with the methods property instead, so that optimization silently never applied to them. This didn't cause a security problem, since the check itself already allows GET, HEAD, OPTIONS and TRACE requests, but it meant the check was being unnecessarily evaluated on read-only routes defined the modern way. The fix drops the outdated, partially broken logic and instead declares the check statically for any route that has the _csrf_request_header_token requirement, regardless of how its methods are declared.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Drupal\Core\Access\CsrfRequestHeaderAccessCheck now implements Drupal\Core\Routing\Access\AccessInterface instead of AccessCheckInterface; its applies(Route $route) method has been removed.

Technical details

Previously CsrfRequestHeaderAccessCheck implemented AccessCheckInterface, which requires an applies(Route $route) method that Drupal calls dynamically per route to decide whether to attach the checker. That method inspected the deprecated _method route requirement and only skipped attaching the check if all required methods were read-only; routes using the modern methods route property never had _method set, so the method-based skip never kicked in for them.

The fix, following a suggestion from longwood in the thread that the check "doesn't need to be dynamic at all," removes applies() and the _method inspection entirely. CsrfRequestHeaderAccessCheck now implements the plain AccessInterface and is registered in core.services.yml with applies_to: _csrf_request_header_token on its access_check service tag, so Drupal's CheckProvider attaches it statically based purely on the presence of that requirement key. The actual read/write distinction is still enforced at runtime inside access(), which already unconditionally allows GET, HEAD, OPTIONS and TRACE requests before checking for the CSRF token header. A new kernel test, CsrfRequestHeaderAccessCheckTest, asserts the checker is attached to routes declaring _csrf_request_header_token regardless of their declared methods, and not attached when the requirement is absent.

Upgrade

If custom code extends CsrfRequestHeaderAccessCheck or type-hints against AccessCheckInterface specifically for this class, update to the new contract: implement Drupal\Core\Routing\Access\AccessInterface and rely on the applies_to service tag attribute instead of overriding applies(). For example, in a service definition:

access_check.header.csrf:
  class: Drupal\Core\Access\CsrfRequestHeaderAccessCheck
  arguments: ['@session_configuration', '@csrf_token']
  tags:
    - { name: access_check, applies_to: _csrf_request_header_token, needs_incoming_request: TRUE }

Routes that rely on this checker should also prefer the methods route property over the deprecated _method requirement key.

  • Committed: July 28, 2026 (3 months later)
